hints.title: Pattern Criteria Mapping
hints.text: Analyze each of the four required boolean conditions on the sequence: start codon prefix, stop codon suffix, repeating dinucleotide substring, and triple guanine substring.

hints.title: Conditional Flag Generation
hints.text: Use conditional statements with string pattern functions or regular expressions to produce binary indicator flags.

hints.title: Ascending Identifier Order
hints.text: Project the original identifier, sequence, species, and the four flags ordered by sample_id ascending.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    sample_id, 
    dna_sequence, 
    species,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE 'ATG%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_start,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence REGEXP 'TAA$|TAG$|TGA$' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_stop,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE '%ATAT%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_atat,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE '%GGG%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_ggg
FROM Samples
ORDER BY sample_id;
```

variables: n: number of rows in Samples table
L: length of DNA sequence string
complexity.notes: Scans each sequence and checks string patterns and regular expression markers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full table scan is required as string contents cannot use index lookups for internal substrings.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct conditional pattern evaluations avoid multi-table joins.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use concise SQL expressions to evaluate multiple distinct pattern flags simultaneously.

SELECT 
    sample_id, 
    dna_sequence, 
    species,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE 'ATG%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_start,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence REGEXP 'TAA$|TAG$|TGA$' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_stop,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE '%ATAT%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_atat,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE '%GGG%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_ggg
FROM Samples
ORDER BY sample_id;

SELECT 
    sample_id, 
    dna_sequence, 
    species,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE 'ATG%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_start,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence ~ '(TAA|TAG|TGA)$' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_stop,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE '%ATAT%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_atat,
    CASE WHEN dna_sequence LIKE '%GGG%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_ggg
FROM Samples
ORDER BY sample_id;

import pandas as pd

def dna_pattern_recognition(samples: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = samples.copy()
    df['has_start'] = df['dna_sequence'].str.startswith('ATG').astype(int)
    df['has_stop'] = df['dna_sequence'].str.contains(r'(?:TAA|TAG|TGA)$', regex=True).astype(int)
    df['has_atat'] = df['dna_sequence'].str.contains('ATAT', regex=False).astype(int)
    df['has_ggg'] = df['dna_sequence'].str.contains('GGG', regex=False).astype(int)
    return df.sort_values(by='sample_id', ascending=True)
